title: Treasury liquidity-support buyback operation (TIPS 1-10Y, $750M cap, 1:40pm ET)
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Buyback Operations (August 2026 refunding, masthead 'For Publication August 5, 2026'), PDF re-fetched and its text layer independently decompressed 2026-09-08 (plain curl, HTTP 200, 125,547 bytes, md5 79b65955e74a59f6bebff3adf8ba7b35 — byte-identical to the 09-03/09-05/09-06/09-08 fetches on the sibling buyback ledgers) — the row reads verbatim announce 9/28/2026, operation 9/29/2026 1:40 pm - 2:00 pm, settle 9/30/2026, Liquidity Support, TIPS 1Y to 10Y, maturity range 09/30/2027 - 09/29/2036, min $0, max $750 million. Estimate, not confirmed, on the two counts every buyback row off this document carries: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and the confirming primary is the 09-28 operation announcement rather than this document. Re-checked 2026-09-08
notes: CANONICAL FILE written 2026-09-08 during this event's own initial research, from the one proposal that existed for the id (from-treasury-buyback-tips-10y30y-2026-09-15, filed the same day); that proposal's read is upheld and sharpened. THE FINDING THAT MAKES IT WORTH TRACKING, off api.fiscaldata.treasury.gov buybacks_operations (all 220 operations, both pages, fetched 2026-09-08): this is the ONLY TIPS bucket in the program whose cap actually binds — 7 of 8 operations filled 98-100% of the $750M cap, a 93.7% mean fill that ranks 4th of the program's 15 bucket/type categories, against 22.5% (0 of 4) for its TIPS 10Y-30Y sibling and 10.3% (0 of 9) for the 7Y-10Y nominal bucket. The streak broke on 2026-07-22: $405M accepted, a 54.0% fill, on $3,194M offered (12.7% take share). That is the program's ONLY uncensored measurement of this bucket's price-acceptable supply — the other seven are censored at the cap — and it reads BELOW the cap. The mechanism is measurable rather than inferred: total par offered has fallen $6,512M -> $3,194M (-51%) across the eight operations while the maturity window's front rolled a full year (2026-10-15 -> 2027-10-15) and the count of eligible sub-1%-coupon lines fell 14 -> 10. Structurally this is also the only buyback bucket that mixes all four TIPS tenors ever issued: its 27-line July list spans original 30-Year TIPS auctioned 1998-04-08 and 1999-04-07, 20-Year TIPS from 2008/2009, negative-real-yield 10-Year TIPS from 2020-2022, and 5-Year TIPS from 2024/2025 — 27 years of issuance vintage, the exact inverse of the 10Y-30Y bucket, which contains only 30-year paper. Two schedule firsts: 09-29 settles 09/30/2026, the last business day of September AND of Q3 (no prior operation in this bucket settled on a month-end business day), and the August-refunding schedule gives this bucket two rows ($750M each, 9/29 and 10/21) against one $500M TIPS 10Y-30Y row. sb0607 (fetched direct 2026-09-08, HTTP 200) names 'nominal coupon securities' only, so this $750M cap is untouched inside the 09-09 -> 11-04 doubled window. Low impact is honest about size: ~$45B of TIPS issuance is scheduled in the same corridor (09-17 10Y reopening, 10-22 new 5Y), a 60:1 issuance-to-cap ratio. Estimate-labelled; nothing here licenses an entry. Full workup: docs/research/events/treasury-buyback-tips-1y10y-2026-09-29.md
